claims.text: Oxymetazoline q8–12h; max 5 days, or 3 days on / 3 days off until the sinusitis resolves
claims.quote: Topical decongestants (vasoconstrictors), such as phenylephrine 0.25% spray every 3 hours or oxymetazoline every 8 to 12 hours, are effective but should be used for a maximum of 5 days or for a repeating cycle of 3 days on and 3 days off until the sinusitis is resolved.

claims.text: Use for longer than 3 days can cause rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa)
claims.quote: Use of topical vasoconstrictors for periods longer than 3 days can result in rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa).

claims.text: Phenylephrine nasal spray (OTC label): adults and ≥12 y/o, 2–3 sprays/nostril ⍉more often than q4h
claims.quote: adults and children 12 years of age & older: 2 or 3 sprays in each nostril not more often than every 4 hours
claims.locator: H-E-B Nasal Spray (phenylephrine HCl 1%), Drug Facts

claims.quote: do not use for more than 3 days.
claims.locator: H-E-B Nasal Spray (phenylephrine HCl 1%), Drug Facts

claims.quote: children under 12 years of age: ask a doctor
claims.locator: H-E-B Nasal Spray (phenylephrine HCl 1%), Drug Facts

claims.text: Oral phenylephrine: FDA proposes removing it as an OTC nasal decongestant ← ⍉effective
claims.quote: Food and Drug Administration announced it is proposing to remove oral phenylephrine as an active ingredient that can be used in over-the-counter (OTC) monograph drug products for the temporary relief of nasal congestion after an agency review of the available data determined that oral phenylephrine is not effective for this use.
claims.locator: FDA Proposes Ending Use of Oral Phenylephrine as OTC Monograph Nasal Decongestant Active Ingredient After Extensive Review (press announcement)
